title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean (kernel) proves the halting configurations, no halt in the first 10,000 steps (107 with native_decide) and three shift rules. Direct C runs find no halt in 2·1010 steps and show the word-and-counter structure described below; the map of the left-end rebuilds, which is where a halt could happen, is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: W 0 1^3 0 1^(2k+1) B>0 0 → W 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 C> 0^(2k) 1 (head on the first of the 2k 0s) in 2k+11 steps (the last block erased after a record); B> (10)^k → (01)^k B> and B> (01)^k → (11)^k B> in 2k steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 214 cells have been visited and 112 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Direct C runs (tools/c/tmrun.c, and c/fevents.c of 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC---) reach 2·1010 steps; there are 133 F events (A reading 1), each followed by a 0.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/fixed
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.071).

claims.title: Records are words; time doubles
claims.text: At every record of the first 2·1010 steps outside the left-end rebuilds the tape is a word ending in 1^n B>0, n grows by 2 per record (to 51), the rest changes by one local rewrite, and the time between records tends to double.

claims.title: Halting only at the left end
claims.text: A reads a 1 (the only way to F) only while the left end of the word is rebuilt, after the moving rewrite has reached it (some of these rebuilds are restarts of the last block).
claims.where: F events of the direct run

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The record-to-record map and the map of the left-end rebuilds have not been derived, so there is no accelerated simulation beyond direct runs.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine writes a word of blocks of 1s whose last block grows by 2 at every record while the time between records doubles; it could only stop during rare rebuilds of the left end of the word, and none of the few seen so far did.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run; 133 F events.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Last block of the word at the last record seen.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.071).
After 109 steps the tape spans 214 cells (27 left of the start, 184 right), with a density of 1s of 0.523.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: At every record, a word
html: This machine and 1RB1RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_0RA0LB_0RB--- differ only in A1 and E0, and they behave the same way. Each time the head reaches a new cell on the right (a record), the tape is a word: blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, ending in 1^n B>0. For this machine, the word starts at the left end of the visited tape. The blocks are odd, except that the first may be 2.

From one record to the next the last block grows by 2. The rest of the word changes by one small, width-preserving rewrite, at a place that moves one block to the left per record. The rewrites seen are 3 1 1 → 1 1 3, b → (b−2) 1, 5 1 1 → 3 1 3, 3 3 3 1 1 1 → 1 1 3 5 3 and a few others. The time between records tends to double. In the first 2·1010 steps the last block reaches 51 (record at step 1.57·1010).

sections.heading: Two counters
html: Right after a record, state D erases the last block from right to left. Only a single marker 1 remains, n+1 cells out. This is the Lean theorem rec_erase: W 0 1^3 0 1^(2k+1) B>0 0 becomes W 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 C> 0^(2k) 1 (the head on the first of the 2k 0s) in 2k+11 steps. The head then zigzags. Going left, it turns the single-1 blocks at the end of the word into units 1 1 0 0. Going right, B sweeps them back, turning 10 into 01 and 01 into 11 (b_sweep10, b_sweep01). Meanwhile the empty stretch fills with gaps 1 0^odd.

Between two records of 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB---, the turning points follow a ruler sequence on both sides of a fixed cell. On the right they go 88, 90, 88, 92, 88, 90, 88, 94, …. On the left they dig 55, 65, 41, 65, 55, 65, 45, … cells deep into the word. This is the signature of two binary counters running against each other: one written in the end of the word, one in the gaps. A full count takes about 2n/2 steps, and it ends at the next record.

sections.heading: Rebuilds and F events
html: F is reached only from A reading a 1, and F halts on a 1. So a halt needs A to read 1 1. In the runs, A reads a 1 only when the moving rewrite reaches the left end of the word. There the machine rebuilds the left end. Some of these rebuilds also extend the word, and the last block starts again small (a restart). Records during a rebuild need not be words, and the F events come in bursts there. In the first 2·1010 steps there are 133 F events, and each is followed by a 0.

Rebuilds are rare. For 1RB0RF_1RC0RA_1LD1RB_1LE0LD_1LB0LB_0RB--- the restarts come at about 5·103, 1.4·104, 3.1·105, 1.5·107, 9.7·107 and 7.0·109 steps. They are rare because the rewrite moves one block per record and records come ever more slowly, so direct simulation sees only a handful. Deciding the machine needs the exact record-to-record map on words, and from it the map of the left-end rebuilds. Neither is written down yet.
Status: open. Lean has the halting configurations, no halt in 107 steps, and three shift rules of the sweeps. The record structure is observed in direct runs, not proved.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: At every record a word of blocks with a last block growing by 2 and doubling time; halting only possible at rare rebuilds of the left end; open.
